# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to `BACKLOG.md` as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs or GitHub issues
  (rule 14; owner decision 2026-10-22 at mission approval).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

<skill name="user-testing-validator" filePath="builtin:user-testing-validator">
# User Testing Validator

You validate a milestone by testing the application through its **real user surface** -- the same interface an actual user would interact with. The goal is to verify that the built features work as a user would experience them. You handle setup, determine what needs testing, spawn flow validators via Task tool, and synthesize results.

## Where things live

**missionDir** (path shown in bootstrap):
| File | Purpose | Precedence |
|------|---------|------------|
| `AGENTS.md` (§ Testing & Validation Guidance) | User/orchestrator testing guidance | Must remain consistent with user-approved scope; generated guidance is not itself user approval |
| `validation-contract.md` | Assertion definitions (what to test) | |
| `validation-state.json` | Assertion pass/fail status | |
| `features.json` | Feature list with `fulfills` mapping | |
| `library/user-testing.md` | Discovered testing knowledge (tools, URLs, setup steps, quirks). Read and update as you learn. May not exist yet — create it if needed. | |
| `services.yaml` | Service definitions (start/stop/healthcheck). Update if corrections needed. | |
| `validation/<milestone>/user-testing/` | Synthesis and flow reports (output) | |

## 0) Identify your milestone and check for prior runs

Your feature ID is `user-testing-validator-<milestone>`. Extract the milestone name.

Check if a previous user testing synthesis exists:
```bash
MILESTONE="..."
SYNTHESIS_FILE="{missionDir}/validation/$MILESTONE/user-testing/synthesis.json"
if [ -f "$SYNTHESIS_FILE" ]; then
  cat "$SYNTHESIS_FILE"
fi
```

If it exists, this is a **re-run after fixes**. Test failed/blocked assertions and affected regression paths (see re-run logic below).

Follow explicit user-approved testing requirements. If generated guidance conflicts with them or adds a materially stronger assurance requirement, surface the conflict to the orchestrator rather than silently adopting or dropping it. Do not infer user authorization just from a requirement appearing in AGENTS.md.

## 1) Determine testable assertions

### First run (no prior synthesis)

Collect assertions from features' `fulfills` field:

```bash
jq --arg m "$MILESTONE" '
  .features
  | map(select(.milestone == $m and .status == "completed"))
  | map(select(.skillName // "" | test("^scrutiny-|^user-testing-") | not))
  | map(.fulfills // [])
  | flatten
  | unique
' {missionDir}/features.json
```

Cross-reference with `validation-state.json`: only include assertions that are currently `"pending"`.

### Re-run (prior synthesis exists)

Collect assertions to test from TWO sources:

1. **Failed/blocked from prior synthesis:**
   - Extract `failedAssertions` and `blockedAssertions` from the prior synthesis

2. **New assertions from fix features:**
   - Check features completed AFTER the prior synthesis
   - Collect their `fulfills` for any NEW assertion IDs not yet in `validation-state.json` as `"passed"`

Test the union of both sets. If the union is empty (prior round didn't test anything, e.g., setup consumed the session), treat this as a first run.

Also retest previously passed assertions whose behavior or evidence validity was affected by the fixes. Reuse unaffected evidence with its source and limitations; do not require a new proof system to prove that earlier reports existed.

### No assertions left to test

If, after collecting from the rules above, the set of assertions you need to test is empty (all in-scope assertions have still-valid passing evidence, or remaining assertions were deferred with user authorization):
- Skip Steps 2-6.
- In Step 7, write a synthesis with `status: "pass"`, `assertionsSummary` totals reflecting 0 newly-tested assertions, and a `salientSummary` explaining that there was nothing in scope to test this round.
- Proceed to Step 8 and call `EndFeatureRun` with `successState: "success"`.

## 2) Setup (start services, seed data)

Read all files listed in "Where things live" above.

Start all services needed for testing:
- Check `depends_on` and start dependencies first
- Run each service's `start` command
- Wait for `healthcheck` to pass

Seed any test data needed per `user-testing.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

**Testing tools:** Each assertion in the validation contract specifies its tool explicitly (e.g., `agent-browser`, `tuistory`, `curl`). If not, figure out what's appropriate and document it in `user-testing.md` for your subagents and future runs. Check `{missionDir}/library/user-testing.md` and `{missionDir}/AGENTS.md` for additional tool setup or configuration guidance.

Built-in skills your subagents can invoke via the Skill tool:
- `agent-browser` -- browser automation for web UI testing (navigation, screenshots, form interaction)
- `tuistory` -- terminal automation for CLI/TUI testing (snapshots, keyboard interaction)

For API testing, `curl` works directly. The project may also have its own testing tools or skills.

**External dependencies:** Use real integrations as approved. Mock an external boundary only when the user authorized it or real testing is genuinely impossible and the limitation is reported to the orchestrator. Never silently replace explicitly required real-integration evidence with a mock. Never mock the application's own services to claim end-to-end success; the core application must run for real.

**Internal/fault assertions:** Use the appropriate approved direct integration or deterministic fault test for internal invariants that have no user surface. Record what it exercised and what it did not. Do not build new production-facing fault selectors just for validation. If a contract requires a different evidence level, report the gap to the orchestrator rather than silently marking it passed.

**If setup issues arise**, try to resolve them — fix broken healthchecks, adjust ports, correct seed scripts, create test fixtures or seed data if missing. Do NOT modify production/business logic to work around setup issues (e.g., don't disable auth because login is hard to test).

If you resolve setup issues, update `{missionDir}/library/user-testing.md` with what you learned or set up and `{missionDir}/services.yaml` if service definitions need correction. Track these in your synthesis as `appliedUpdates`.

If setup consumed your session and you couldn't get to actual testing, proceed to Step 7 (synthesis) and return failure — a fresh validator will pick up where you left off with the updated guides. If you were unable to resolve setup issues to unblock testing, return failure with details about what's broken.

## 3) Plan isolation and concurrency strategy

### 3a) Read resource cost classification

Check `{missionDir}/library/user-testing.md` for the `## Validation Concurrency` section. The orchestrator set a **max concurrent validators** number for each surface based on readiness-check observations. Treat this as the resource ceiling — do not exceed it.

If this section doesn't exist, or doesn't include a surface one of your assertions uses, make your own resource cost assessment based on the testing tools and services involved and set a max concurrency (1-5). Reason about what validators will actually trigger — worker threads, background jobs, or specific user flows can all spike resource usage well beyond what current machine metrics suggest. Document your assessment in `user-testing.md` for future runs.

### 3b) Assess current machine state

```bash
# Memory and CPU
vm_stat  # macOS — look at "Pages free" and "Pages active"
sysctl -n hw.memsize  # macOS — total physical memory
# Use a platform-appropriate process listing to identify top memory consumers
# (for example: ps, top, or Activity Monitor on macOS)
```

### 3c) Analyze isolation

For each surface, determine whether validators can operate concurrently without interfering. Think from first principles about what shared state the assertions you're testing actually touch:

- Validators using separate user accounts / namespaces / data directories against shared infrastructure can typically run concurrently without conflict.
- Assertions that mutate global state (e.g., global settings, shared database rows, singleton resources) will interfere if run concurrently — group them together or serialize them.

### 3d) Final parallelization decision

## 0
# User testing

**What belongs here:** the surfaces a validator can drive, the exact commands that worked on this machine
(validation readiness report, 2026-10-22), the oracle commands, the evidence to collect, the cost class of
each surface and how validators isolate from each other. Sections marked "to be filled by validators"
collect runtime findings as milestones land.

**What does not belong here:** start/stop/healthcheck commands and ports (`services.yaml`), machine facts
(`environment.md`), Rust test conventions (`rust-conventions.md`).

## Surfaces at a glance

| Surface | What it proves | Driver | Cost class |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI (`observatory-cli replay`, `inspect`, `metrics --csv`) and `cargo test` | mapping, counts, pointers, metrics; the oracle for everything else | shell | low (warm `cargo test` 2.6 s in the scratch crate) |
| Browser host: `trunk serve` on 3141 | the board and every view-model in a real browser (primary interactive surface, SPEC §6) | `agent-browser` | medium: trunk 35 MB idle, each browser session 1.34-1.54 GB RSS, max 3 sessions |
| Tauri window: `make app-dev` | the native shell starts, loads the same UI, wires commands (smoke check, planning note 4) | `ps`, log, `lsof`, `osascript`, `screencapture` | high during the build (37.66 s to the app process, native rustc burst), low idle (130 MB RSS) |
| Live attach / host | a real `droid exec --mission` appears on the board within 1 s (M1), hosted mission controls (M2) | terminal + board | medium (a Droid session plus the board) |
| `cargo llvm-cov` | coverage floor | shell | high: load 3.3 to 14.6 on 10 cores; runs alone |
| GitHub via `gh api` | PR, runs, statuses, rulesets for the gate lane (M4) | `gh` | low |

Serialize anything that compiles: cargo builds share the `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock; `cargo llvm-cov` and the
first `cargo tauri dev` build run with nothing else compiling. Validators run user tests only after builds
finish.

## Browser host (primary)

Start `trunk-ui` from `services.yaml` and wait for `curl -sf http://localhost:3141/` (55.94 s cold, then
1.46-2.08 s per incremental rebuild). Then, exactly as they worked on 2026-10-22:

```sh
until curl -sf -o /dev/null http://localhost:3141/; do sleep 1; done
agent-browser open http://localhost:3141          # 1.25 s
agent-browser snapshot                            # accessibility tree with refs: heading ... [ref=e1], button ... [ref=e2]
agent-browser snapshot -i                         # interactive elements only
agent-browser click @e2                           # click by ref
agent-browser get title
agent-browser get text body
agent-browser screenshot /tmp/observatory-<milestone>-<scenario>.png
agent-browser console                             # expect empty
agent-browser errors                              # expect empty
agent-browser --session <name> open http://localhost:3141   # isolated second validator (own Chrome, own page state)
agent-browser session list
agent-browser close --all                         # at the end; daemons otherwise linger 1 h
```

Rules:

- One `--session <name>` per validator (`default` is a session too); at most 3 sessions per `trunk serve`;
  never more than 5. Sessions are isolated (verified: `clicks: 1` in `default` while `val2` showed `clicks: 0`).
- Read the page through `snapshot`, not the raw HTML: the dev page carries trunk's live-reload script
  (websocket `/.well-known/trunk/ws`) at the top of `<body>`; the app is inside `<main>`.
- Evidence per scenario: the snapshot lines you asserted on (with refs), the screenshot path and byte size
  (`Screenshot saved to ... (12217 bytes)` style), `console` and `errors` output, and the CLI oracle output
  for the same fixture.
- `agent-browser` cannot attach to the Tauri window (no CDP endpoint; `connect 9229` fails with
  `All CDP discovery methods failed`). A failed `connect` leaves a daemon entry; close it.

### Opening a fixture in the browser host

The UI's `BrowserBackend` (architecture §7) reads the fixture through an `<input type=file>` file picker,
runs `mapping::map_record` and `core::view` in wasm, with no store. The exact agent-browser steps (which ref
the input has, which command sets a file on it, whether a `.capture.json` or the root `.jsonl` is picked,
how the children directory is supplied) are not known until the UI exists.

**To be filled by the M1 ui-worker:** the exact commands, the expected `MissionSummary` text on screen
(`event_count`, `unknown_count`, `mapping_version`) and the fixture used
(`fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl`).

## Tauri window (smoke check)

Owner decision (planning note 4): the Tauri window is validated as a smoke check; the functional evidence is
the browser host. Procedure, with the commands that worked:

1. Make sure no other trunk owns 3141 (`lsof -nP -iTCP:3141 -sTCP:LISTEN`, exit 1 = free), then start
   `tauri-dev` from `services.yaml` (log `/tmp/observatory-tauri.log`). Start it (and any `trunk serve`)
   with Execute `fireAndForget: true`; a `nohup ... &` in a normal call dies when the call returns
   (observed by the s-app-empty-lanes worker). `make app-dev` passed this smoke set on 2026-10-22
   (cargo-tauri, trunk, observatory-app PIDs; WebKit ESTABLISHED to [::1]:3141).
2. Wait for the line `Running /home/user/.cargo/shared_rust_target/debug/observatory-app` in the log
   (37.66 s after launch with warm wasm; 31.18 s of it is the native build) and check that no panic follows.
3. Process alive:

   ```sh
   ps -axo pid,command | awk '$2 ~ /shared_rust_target\/debug\/observatory-app$/ {print $1}'
   ps -p <pid> -o pid,rss,%cpu,command          # 130 MB RSS, 0.0 %CPU idle in the readiness run
   ```

4. The webview fetched the page: `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141` shows `com.apple.WebKit` (or `com.apple ...`)
   `ESTABLISHED` connections to `[::1]:3141` (three in the readiness run).
5. System Events lists the app as a foreground process:

   ```sh
   osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to get name of every process whose background only is false'
   osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to get {name, unix id, frontmost, visible} of process "observatory-app"'
   osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to tell process "observatory-app" to count windows'   # 1 when the display is unlocked
   ```

6. Screenshot only when the display is unlocked: check
   `ioreg -n Root -d1 -a | grep -A1 CGSSessionScreenIsLocked` first; locked gives a uniformly black frame
   (`YAVG=16`) and `count windows` 0. Then `screencapture -x /tmp/observatory-tauri-<milestone>.png` and verify
   with `ffmpeg -hide_banner -i <png> -vf signalstats,metadata=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:file=- -f null - 2>/dev/null | grep YAVG`.
   If the display is locked, record process/log/System-Events evidence and say so; the owner's screenshot
   (below) is the human-captured frame.
7. Shutdown: kill cargo-tauri, `trunk serve` and the app binary by PID (killing cargo-tauri alone orphans the
   other two, trunk keeps 3141 bound). `services.yaml` `tauri-dev.stop` does this. Confirm with
   `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141 -sTCP:LISTEN` (exit 1) and the System Events list.

Whether a window-level screenshot works on an unlocked screen is unverified (the readiness run had the
screen locked). **To be filled by validators:** the first unlocked `count windows` and `screencapture` result,
with the window title (`app.windows[].title`, `droid-observatory`).

## CLI oracle

All from the worktree (`services.yaml` `replay`, `inspect`, `metrics-csv`):

```sh
cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl        # prints lane events, ends with `unknown events: N`; exit 0
cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay /nonexistent.jsonl; echo $?           # non-zero (cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file)
cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- inspect <event-id>                             # the exact raw bytes of the line by pointer; `--scrub` applies the B-006 pass
cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- metrics fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl --csv # M5; compared to reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv within 1 s, 1 token, 0.01 USD
make replay-fixtures                                                              # every fixture, exit 1 on the first failure
```

The last line of `replay` and the tray count on the board must agree; `inspect` output must equal the
byte slice `dd if=<file> bs=1 skip=<byte_offset> count=<byte_len>` of the fixture. M0 gate: `unknown events: 0`
on the M0 capture; S allows N > 0.

## Store

`[store].path` defaults to `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite`; a validator overrides it through a temp
config (`OBSERVATORY_CONFIG=<path>`, see Isolation). Inspect read-only:

```sh
sqlite3 -readonly ~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite '.tables'
sqlite3 -readonly ~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite 'select count(*) from events;'
sqlite3 -readonly ~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite 'select * from mapping_versions; select * from captures;'
```

# Validation contract — mission `observatory-v1`

## Sources and precedence

This contract is synthesized from the seven area drafts in `contract-work/` (`skel.md`, `map.md`, `board.md`,
`host-control.md`, `gate.md`, `metrics.md`, `cross-process.md`). Where sources disagree the order is:
`planning-notes.md` (owner decisions after the spec, binding) > `SPEC.md` v0.2 > `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`
v0.6. `architecture.md` is the design reference: assertions whose only source is the architecture (file layouts,
log line names, config defaults not yet in `config/observatory.example.toml`, exact UI strings) are kept and
tagged `(source: architecture)` in their description; a worker who changes that design detail must change the
assertion through the orchestrator, not fail it silently. Numbers are the sources' numbers, pasted, never
estimated (RULES rule 7). Repository: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`; worktrees
`/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/<m>` on branch `wt/<m>` for `<m>` in `s`, `m0`,
`m1`, `m2`, `m3`, `m4`, `m5`; `<wt/m>` below means that worktree root.

## Evidence conventions

Each assertion ends with `Tool:` (one word from the vocabulary below) and `Evidence:` (a comma-separated list of
artifacts the validator attaches). Evidence items use these forms:

- `screenshot(<name>)` — a PNG taken by `agent-browser screenshot` (browser host) or, for the Tauri window, the
  owner's unlocked-display screenshot named `owner-screenshot(<path>)`.
- `snapshot(<name>)` — the text of `agent-browser snapshot` (accessibility tree) at that moment.
- `console-errors` — the output of `agent-browser console` and `agent-browser errors` (expected empty unless stated).
- `terminal-output(<command or what>)` — the pasted stdout/stderr and exit code of a shell command.
- `gh-output(<what>)` — pasted `gh` / `gh api` output with the command that produced it.
- `app-log(<what>)` — lines from the Tauri shell's tracing output (`make app-dev` redirected to a file).
- `sqlite-query(<SQL or what>)` — pasted `sqlite3` query and result against `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite`
  (or the scratch store named by `OBSERVATORY_CONFIG`).
- `file(<path>)` — the file (or the quoted excerpt) at the named path and commit.
- `git-log(<range or what>)` — pasted `git log` / `git diff` / `git worktree` output with the command.

## Tool vocabulary

`git`, `shell`, `make`, `cargo test`, `cli` (`observatory-cli replay|inspect|metrics`), `agent-browser`,
`tauri-smoke`, `sqlite3`, `gh`, `file` (report or document inspection).

## Surface rules (planning note 4)

- The browser host is the primary interactive surface: `trunk serve --config apps/observatory-app/ui/Trunk.toml
  --port 3141 --open false` from the active worktree, driven by `agent-browser --session <name>` (at most 3
  sessions per `trunk serve`, SPEC §5.8), the fixture opened through the file picker. Cold `trunk serve` is
  55.94 s, incremental 1.46–2.08 s.
- The Tauri window (`make app-dev`, 37.66 s to a running app) is a smoke check: the `observatory-app` process is
  alive, the dev log has the `Running .../debug/observatory-app` line with no `panicked` after it,
  `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141` lists `com.apple.WebKit` connections, System Events lists the app. Exactly one `trunk` owns
  3141 at a time: stop the standalone `trunk serve` before `make app-dev`; stop `cargo-tauri`, `trunk` and the app
  binary by PID afterwards. The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; what happens inside it is evidenced by the app
  log, the store, the CLI and the owner screenshot.
- At each milestone integration the owner takes one real screenshot with the display unlocked; its path is
  recorded in the boundary report and the session log (VAL-PROC-019).
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone; cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock (waits, not failures).
- Attach and host run only in the Tauri shell (the browser backend has no watcher, store or child process); the
  GitHub poll runs only in the Tauri shell. Scripted attach cases use `OBSERVATORY_CONFIG=<tmp>/config.toml` with
  `[ingest].factory_sessions_dir` pointing at a temp directory so `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written.
- Process assertions (worktree identity, red-before-green, `make check` in the worktree, coverage, commit rules,
  must-not-touch scope, Tauri smoke at m1–m5, fixture gitleaks) live once in the Process section with their
  milestone populations; area sections keep only milestone-specific gates.

## Area: S — Walking skeleton (milestone s)

Validator notes. Sources: planning notes 1, 3, 4, 5, 9, 11; architecture §1–6, §14–16; SPEC §3 "Common" and "S",
§6–8; `Makefile`; `.github/workflows/{mission-branch,release,bundle}.yml`; AGENTS.md; PRD §7. Fixed populations:
the nine lanes in PRD §7 order (`Intent`, `Orchestrator`, `Workers`, `Validators, scrutiny`, `Validators, user
testing`, `Integration`, `Human`, `Outside`, `Time, Waste, Cost and models`); the six S tests
(`replay_counts_every_line_of_a_capture`, `unknown_event_keeps_raw_type_and_byte_offset`,
`event_round_trips_through_serde`, `lanes_are_nine_in_prd_order`, `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file`,
`every_event_carries_the_mapping_version`); the S fixture `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` with

to VAL-PROC-010.

### VAL-SKEL-001: `make doctor` reports no missing required tool

`(source: architecture §15)` `.github/workflows/bundle.yml` in `wt/s` has an `install-action` step whose `tool:` lists `trunk@0.22.0` and `tauri-cli@2.12.4` (the versions in SPEC §4 / the dependency readiness report) and a step running `make app-build BUNDLES=app,dmg` (or `cargo tauri build --bundles app,dmg`), while the local `tauri.conf.json` keeps `bundle.targets: ["app"]` (VAL-SKEL-012; planning note 3). `make check-workflows` passes. `git clone --branch wt/s <repo-url-or-local-path> /tmp/skel-clean` (and, at the S integration, the same clone checked out at the `s` integration commit on `mission/observatory-v1`), then in the clone: `make doctor` shows no `missing` line, `make hooks` exits 0, `make check` exits 0, `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` exits 0 with the last line `unknown events: N` (same N as VAL-SKEL-005), using only commands documented in `README.md` "From a clean clone" and `AGENTS.md` "Interactive QA path" (SPEC §3 S exit criterion, rule 5).
